rule: A creature's moves are an ordered list of mobskill slots. Each slot has its own percent roll (TriRnd), optional HP trigger (TriHp, fires at or below that percent of own HP), a use cap (TriCount), and a payload (skill, summon, poly, or melee range). The engine walks the slots in order, skips any slot that is not usable, and the first slot that performs ends the turn. Pack wake: a hit on a monster with wake mode 1 sets every known monster with the same family id to engage, and monsters in the same mob group join too; wake mode 0 means no wake. Escort groups: a leader plus up to six escort kinds, each with a count, and an optional remove-on-leader-death flag. Defect: the roll is nextInt(100)+1 compared with a strict less-than, so TriRnd 100 fires 99 percent of the time, TriRnd 2 once in 100, and TriRnd 1 never. Sprites are reused: 1,448 monster rows share 693 sprite ids, and a single sprite can sit on several level bands with hand-set exp and hp.
keep: Ordered move list with a per-move roll and an HP trigger; the first move that passes is the one used.
Family string key that wakes its kin on a hit, with a same-family rule.
Leader with escorts, counts per escort kind, and a leader-death rule.
Sprite reuse by row: one body, many stat rows.
change: Fix the roll to chance <= TriRnd, or roll 0-99 and use <; a fallback slot at 100 should always fire.
Delete the unused wake mode 2 and collapse the wake logic into one place (the base setLink body is empty).
Index family members once at zone load; the current link scan walks known objects on every hit.
Make the summon-at-cap case an explicit data flag (the code spends the turn without summoning).
Set reward per family on purpose; the data keeps exp flat across some level bands and rises in others.
look_test: Target file src/fight/aggro-link.ts (new), parity row 4 (fight loop: aggro, chase, leash). Build one zone with a three-member family and a leader; hit one member. Compare (a) all family members engage at once against (b) only three attack while the rest hold on the leash. On a phone at 375 wide: does the pack wake read as one event, and does the three-attacker cap read clearly? If the wake feels like a cheat, keep it but limit it to a short range.
